newsitem.title: USA: Rule to bar spinal cord in meat out shortly - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Rule to bar spinal cord in meat out shortly - USDA.

text.p: A directive will be issued "in the next several days" to U.S. meat inspectors to make sure spinal cord does not wind up in processed meat, an Agriculture Department official said Wednesday.

The directive would be a precaution against development of "mad cow" disease in the United States. Thomas Billy, head of the Food Safety and Inspection Service, told a House Appropriations subcommittee hearing the directive would be issued "in the next several days."

Lawmakers showed little enthusiasm for a USDA proposal for $390 million in fees on the meat industry to pay for the cost of in-plant inspection. Chairman Joe Skeen, New Mexico Republican, said, "We've been through this exercise before" and noted the administration had yet to offer legislation to authorize the fees.
Rep. Jack Kingston, R-Ga., decried White House budget gimmicks and said they made it "difficult to drum up support for fee increases."
If the fees are approved, Billy said there would be little leeway in drafting regulations so they would be in place when the new fiscal year begins October 1.
